/work/clients/machine-client/src/agent/tail.rs:
    1|       |//! Server-minted transcript positions. A position is a byte offset that ends
    2|       |//! a complete source line plus a session-bound hash of all bytes before it.
    3|       |//! A tail from an acknowledged offset reads only the source bytes after it;

  560|       |    enum Op {
  561|       |        Open,
  562|       |        Write,
  563|       |        Read,
  564|       |        Screen,
  565|       |        Resize,
  566|       |        Close,
  567|       |        List,
  568|       |    }

  570|     30|    async fn failure_of(pty: &Pty, root: &std::path::Path, op: Op) -> String {
  571|     30|        let name = json!({"name":"sample"});
  572|     30|        match op {
  573|      5|            Op::Open => failure(
  574|      5|                pty.open(
  575|      5|                    &request(json!({"name":"sample","cwd":root})),
  576|      5|                    &[root.to_owned()],
  577|      5|                )
  578|      5|                .await,
  579|       |            ),
  580|      5|            Op::Write => failure(
  581|      5|                pty.write(&request(json!({"name":"sample","data":"eA=="})))
  582|      5|                    .await,
  583|       |            ),
  584|      4|            Op::Read => failure(pty.read(&request(name)).await),
  585|      6|            Op::Screen => failure(
  586|      6|                pty.screen(&request(json!({"name":"sample","source":"screen"})))
  587|      6|                    .await,
  588|       |            ),
  589|      6|            Op::Resize => failure(
  590|      6|                pty.resize(&request(json!({"name":"sample","cols":80,"rows":24})))
  591|      6|                    .await,
  592|       |            ),
  593|      3|            Op::Close => failure(pty.close(&request(name)).await),
  594|      1|            Op::List => failure(pty.list().await),
  595|       |        }
  596|     30|    }

  598|       |    /// A terminal whose `pattern` command answers `%error` with `nope`;
  599|       |    /// `pane` pre-registers `sample` (attached when the pane is known).
  600|     25|    async fn failing(
  601|     25|        pattern: &str,
  602|     25|        extra: &str,
  603|     25|        pane: Option<Option<&str>>,
  604|     25|    ) -> (tempfile::TempDir, Pty) {
  605|     25|        let (root, pty) = terminal(&format!(
  606|     25|            "{pattern}) printf 'nope\\n'; outcome=error ;; {extra}"
  607|     25|        ))
  608|     25|        .await;
  609|     25|        if let Some(pane) = pane {
                                  ^23
  610|     23|            let mut registry = pty.registry.lock().await;
  611|     23|            let record = registry.register("sample").expect("space");
  612|     23|            record.pane = pane.map(str::to_owned);
  613|     23|            record.window = Some("@1".into());
  614|      2|        }
  615|     25|        (root, pty)
  616|     25|    }

    1|       |//! Window-bound observation (#1689). [`Observations`] holds, per attachment,
    2|       |//! the epoch table (a window's recreations as this peer has seen them), the
    3|       |//! observation id counter and the latest snapshot of each lineage
    4|       |//! `w<pid>-<windowId>-<epoch>`. The id counter outlives [`Observations::forget`],
    5|       |//! so a detach never reissues an id. A complete walk is minted into
    6|       |//! elements whose ref is the element's `role[i]` path; an incomplete walk
    7|       |//! cannot prove a ref unambiguous and mints none. A `since` naming the
    8|       |//! lineage's latest observation answers a diff by ref, or every element
    9|       |//! again when either side holds an element without a ref; anything else is
   10|       |//! stale. An action re-checks the lineage, re-resolves its ref on a fresh
   11|       |//! walk and requires the same unclipped role, label and secure flag, and
   12|       |//! the observer dispatches only on the element it resolved and admitted
   13|       |//! against that identity; a pointer aimed at a ref passes the same fresh
   14|       |//! check and lands on the element's centre in global points. Operations on
   15|       |//! one window run one at a time; different windows do not wait on each
   16|       |//! other.

    2|       |//! capture; at capacity a capture is refused rather than queued. A slot goes
    3|       |//! back to the idle set only when its capture succeeded and no release
    4|       |//! happened meanwhile, so a failed capture, a detach or a memory shed always
    5|       |//! frees the buffers.

    1|       |//! The encoded-video path of a live stream (#1662): RGBA8 frames from the
    2|       |//! screen's frame pool become H.264 access units through openh264 (built
    3|       |//! from its bundled source, so Linux headless and macOS share one encoder).
    4|       |//! [`Budget`] decides on an injected clock which frames are due (the fps
    5|       |//! cap), which must be keyframes (the interval or a receiver's request) and
    6|       |//! what quality the encoder runs at: it adapts under congestion but never
    7|       |//! leaves the bounds the host set. A unit above `max_frame_bytes` is
    8|       |//! dropped, never split, and the next frame is a keyframe.

  101|       |    /// Targets `bitrate` clamped to the bounds; fps and dimension follow its
  102|       |    /// share of the maximum in quarters (fps 1/5..5/5, dimension 4/8..8/8).
  103|       |    /// Only a material change is taken (another fps or dimension, or a
  104|       |    /// bitrate a quarter away), since every retune costs a keyframe. True

  106|     48|    fn target(&mut self, bitrate: u64) -> bool {

  108|     48|        let bitrate = bitrate.clamp(MIN_BITRATE.min(max), max);
  109|     48|        let quarters = (u128::from(bitrate) * 4 / u128::from(max)) as u32;

  113|     48|            dimension: (self.bounds.max_dimension * (quarters + 4) / 8).max(2),
  114|     48|        };
